essay.en: I wanted three kinds of prose in one room: classical Chinese pieces, most of them a page or less, written at a spring gathering, in exile, on a walk at night or in old age; the modern Chinese prose of the 1920s, when Lu Xun, Zhu Ziqing and Xu Dishan were showing what the spoken language could carry; and stories and chapters from Europe and America, from Andersen’s Snow Queen to Thoreau sounding a frozen pond. What they share is attention to a single evening, object or person, set down exactly enough to last. Start with Zhang Dai’s night of snow on West Lake, which takes a minute to read; then Lu Xun’s My Old Home, for its last paragraph about roads; then Chekhov’s The Student, in which a story told by one fire reaches two listeners by another.
essay.zh: 我想把三种散文放进同一间屋子。一是古文，大多不过一页，写于春日的雅集、贬谪的江边、一次夜游，或者暮年；二是二十年代的白话文，那时鲁迅、朱自清、许地山正在证明，口语也撑得起一篇好文章；三是欧美的小说与随笔，从安徒生的《冰雪女王》，到梭罗在结了冰的湖面上放绳测深。它们的共同之处，是把一个夜晚、一件东西或一个人看得很准，写得足以留下来。先读张岱的《湖心亭看雪》，一分钟就能读完；再读鲁迅的《故乡》，为了最后那一段关于路的话；然后读契诃夫的《大学生》：在一堆火边讲出的故事，打动了另一堆火边的两个人。
